# Changelog

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/changelog:3.0 -->

This file records meaningful completed changes in chronological order, newest first. Current state and future work belong in `docs/repo-harness/current-state.md`.

## 2026-11-25

- Added the native Android app DeleLuz 1.0.0 (`app/`, Flutter, shared as a signed APK): connect, power, color, brightness, built-in effects 1-210 and Auto, scenes, music modes, several saved strips with per-phone aliases and per-strip setup, cancel a pending connection, and an About section. Verified on two phones and two strips and published as GitHub release v1.0.0 (`DeleLuz-1.0.0.apk`); screenshots and a showreel are in `docs/app-screens/` (`odd/tasks/deleluz-android.md`).

## 2026-11-24

- Added a microphone sensitivity slider for the strip’s onboard mic and verified it on the real strip from Android.
- Set up the Linux workstation for the LED lab: `adb` (phone authorized, `adb reverse` works), `tshark`, and a Linux Python environment `_tools/.venv-linux` (bleak, pyserial, crcmod, tqdm, capstone); verified a read-only BLE scan and connect to the strip from Linux (`_tools/`, not committed).
- Retook the webapp screenshot checkpoint on an Android phone (fresh install, one saved scene) and fixed the visual defects it showed: consistent percent spacing, a sheet header that keeps Close reachable while scrolling, and an unclipped title focus outline (`docs/webapp-screens/`, `odd/tasks/deleluz-webapp.md` T50, L78-L79)
- Added the Ajustes tab to the webapp (replaces Ayuda; sections Tira, Idioma, Ayuda, Privacidad): strip color order and LED count, typed as a total or calculated per meter, sent as the chip-config frame after a confirmation; verified on the real strip at 100 and 150 LEDs (`odd/tasks/deleluz-webapp.md` T46-T49, L70-L77)
- Decoded the chip-config color-order byte (1-based position in the vendor list) and recorded the per-pixel probes: this DMX03 ignores the vendor graffiti frame and the custom color-list pattern, so segment colors need a custom controller (`docs/PROTOCOL.md`)
- Published the project as a public GitHub repository under the MIT license; stopped tracking `.pi/` and moved superseded designs, the store-links note and the original brief to a local, git-ignored `_archive/` (`odd/tasks/deleluz-webapp.md` L67-L69).
- Reworked the webapp around user-editable content (`odd/tasks/deleluz-webapp.md` T21-T45, L28-L64): customizable quick scenes (2 defaults, up to 6, hold for options, drag to reorder), "Mis escenas" color sequences (gallery cards, editor with wheel, drag-reorder, rename, speed %, intensity), one shared favorites palette (green, yellow, red by default, up to 15, replace/move/delete by drag to the trash), Música as cards, Incluidas as cards, swipe between tabs (wraps), collapsible sections closed by default, Disconnect, status chip in every section, AUTO indicator, privacy and permissions in Help, safer error and deletion handling. Saved custom scenes from the previous version were replaced by "Mis escenas" sequences.

- Removed saved custom scenes ("Mis escenas", the + button and the save sheet) from the webapp at the user's request; Scenes lists only the included scenes and built-in effects (`odd/tasks/deleluz-webapp.md` L34).
- The webapp shows the vendor names of the 210 built-in effects (Color and Scenes), cross-checked against an independent catalog (`odd/tasks/deleluz-webapp.md` T16, L32).
- Polished the webapp: voice modes 1-4 in Color → Efectos integrados → Música (verified on the strip), Home fits short screens 320x568-412x915, symmetric color and scene grids, storage failures never block strip commands, scenes resume cleanly after a late wake-up (`odd/tasks/deleluz-webapp.md` T12-T15, L29-L30).
- Added the phone webapp `webapp/` (Glow Glass design `design/deleluz-webapp/`): connect/reconnect, power, brightness, colors, built-in effects, smooth page scenes with preview, saved scenes, off timer (minutes and seconds) and help; commands every 50 ms; verified on the real strip from Android Chrome (`odd/tasks/deleluz-webapp.md`).
- Confirmed the onboard-mic voice modes 1-4 over BLE from Android Chrome without the vendor app (`docs/PROTOCOL.md`, `odd/tasks/led-lab.md` L53-L54).
- Installed Flutter 3.50.1 and the Android command-line tools as local tooling for a possible native app (`_tools/`, not committed).

## 2026-11-23

- Found why Windows cannot control the strip: the controller's `FFE2` characteristic declaration is malformed and Windows rejects characteristic discovery; the adapter is not the cause (`odd/tasks/led-lab.md` L48).
- Read the chip's RAM and its 3 KB plaintext boot code over the one-wire port; ROM and flash stay unreadable; compared three USB-serial adapters (red one is dead) (`odd/tasks/led-lab.md` L49-L52).
- Documented the LEDDMX-03 device investigation: per-pixel control not found in vendor or public sources; controller identified as a Bluetrum SoC (ROM chip ID `BLUEMATE`) with its one-wire download port on the unpopulated header; flash readout blocked with public tools (`odd/tasks/led-lab.md` L28-L47, `docs/CAPABILITIES.md`).

## 2026-11-22

- Set up the repository harness and the LEDDMX-03 research baseline: captured and documented the BLE protocol (`docs/PROTOCOL.md`), added `tools/leddmx.py` (frame builder with tests), `tools/btsnoop_att.py`, and `tools/apk_strings.py`, plus phone design directions in `design/deleluz-mobile/`.
- Created the minimal repository AI harness and its visible continuity documentation.
